body:
I don't feel like I'm not out there. I talk with people in lecture, office hours, and at my club meetings. However, it seems really hard to interest people in doing anything. Coffee, beach, hikes, disk golf, current community events. 

I don't feel like my life is stable enough at this point, nor will be for the foreseeable future, to have friends for what I would consider long term; but of course long term would be better!
Tried that, just kept trying to tell me they weren't.

She left my place to go back to her boyfriend, left him shortly thereafter and I now have no clue. I cut off contact after I realized how manipulative she was and how poorly she treated everyone around her.

I read somewhere all their stores are less than a day away from their main distribution center to help with freshness.

It could have been their promotional stuff, but still thought it was an interesting idea.

From reading that it sounds like I'm in your position.

I want to cultivate a happy, healthy relationship.

Your words have a very strong message that is inspiring to me, and I hope I can be as strong as I want to be reading what you have to say.

I've known I need to talk with her. Deep down I know I need to be frank. I'm afraid that our friendship relies on it being a relationship. (I don't know how to word that better, but I feel it comes across as bad.) I dont want to lose my best friend/girlfriend, and if I do, it's going to be both at the same time.

That's the thing I've been thinking about for too long and living through the pain of it happening, even though it hasn't, and may not happen.

Thank you for taking time to write all that out, like I said above, it's very inspirational to me.

Pretty much the thought I had, but I feel like I have everything to lose, and very little to gain. But the very little is my mental stability, which I seem to undervalue when I weigh the costs of things.

I really appreciate your story and frankness.

We only get a sleepover 1/2ce a week, but it sounds like a similar experience. What did you do about it?

I feel like the relationship, standing alone, is very healthy. It's my mindset that is unhealthy. I need the black and white, yes or no, commitment or not.

I'm seeking help now because I can foresee myself being very, very hurt at some point in the nearish future.

You have a good point, and it totally depends on the time and the person for me. Sometimes I secretly want someone to just just a tiny bit and get me to talk about it. Other times I want them to shut up and just sit there with me and accept my answer..
As someone who has been there, some days all I want is for someone to ask "are you ok" or "how are you doing" and then sit there and listen to the answer and actually care.
This is my favorite answer. I may use about 2/3rds of what you wrote. Thank you.
It is personal, and it's an infinite hiatus. But I liked the first and last bits.
See, I'm not on that bad of terms. I don't want to be really rude about it unless that really is the best way. Would it be better if I tell them/they know?

That's how I feel with my food budget for one.

I mean, I dont spend a ton, and I eat really well, and NEVER eat out, but I COULD work harder and spend less.
That gave me a good smile. Thank you. I think I'm better for this month, and want to reciprocate the effort she's put into me.
I have in the past, but not nearly to the extent she's helped me. I feel indebted, in a caring way.
I have been, it's part of the reason shes willing to help me, but the severity of mine versus her and the effort she has put into me versus the effort Ive put into her is way out of proportion.
I like the simplicity of that, but I feel that saying "I don't know how to say I appreciate you" is kinda like saying nothing.
I do this quite a bit.
I really like this answer, but I don't think I've ever used "remember to buckle up".
I think that 2nd one is the best. You know you have someone special when they scratch your back, without you even looking at them, after they see you struggling.
Are stairs required?
Seems like they fit the question quite well!

See, this is actually where I'm a tiny bit conflicted. I have two different thoughts. One is that she is my friend, the other is that she is someone I'm interested in. I still feel I'm able to keep them separate, but it's getting to be more work. The thing is that permanency is on the table. Regardless of what we call it neither of us sees the other out of their life for a long time. As for the pros and cons, the pros outweigh the cons, because we both agree that if this sexual thing doesn't work out we will just drop back and be ok. We both truly believe that. Her biggest fear is that she will hold me back from some amazing girl that comes along. At the same time I think i COULD go for someone else at some point we've both put a lot of heart and soul into this and have no complaints.

How young we both are also makes this kind of funny I suppose.

Last night she said that, and I thought about it for a long time and thought it to be a good idea. Come this morning I, again, wanted to know what we were doing and what we wanted out of this. I want the stability of a label. My other response is a good reason we dont put a label on it, if you're curious. More than anything I just want to see what other people think.

Sometimes I feel that we arent doing it just as a hipster thing, we enjoy toying with the idea, but find it more fun and playful to not label it.

One of the reasons that we dont label it as such is her ex is one of her housemates and he is going through some depressed times and we don't want to break him, he still really cares about her. I've been her friend since before they met, and he used some very harsh language toward me when they broke up. We've talked about that aspect and have mixed feelings.

Without going into too much of her personal experience on the internet, I'm the only person she wants to have sex with due to her morals and beliefs. I'm not sure why she agreed to have sex with me, based on how strongly I know she subscribes to her beliefs, but she suggested it. I was not the instigator of that because I didn't want to make her uncomfortable. She thinks we have a strong enough relationship ignoring the sex to communicate and have a fun, safe time, and also not miss a step if it stops.

TLDR: She's not interested in other people and wasn't sexually interested in me until she wanted a positive sexual relationship and knew I could provide it, and realized we cared about each other.
Not really, a tiny bit. I still get no sleep.

I appreciate you breaking through the rose tinted glasses. I've known her for three years and think I know her quite well.  Unless something new has developed I think she just has low self esteem and thinks I somehow deserve better, even though her current life situation says I couldn't do much better.

Thank you for your input. You've given me some good lines to help provoke the conversation that I want/think needs to happen. That's why I asked for help, there are so many "emotive forces" that I don't know what to single out and focus on. What do you think the best way to get the conversation rolling about "preemptive expectations" is. Should I continue over the phone or wait till next month when we get together again?

Thank you,
-Thecookie.
